Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The test testLargeSample is failing in the context of fitting polynomials of degrees up to 9 on a large sample of 40,000 points. The failure is relevant to the current bug report about new multivariate vector optimizers not handling large numbers of weights efficiently—in particular, they create a full nxn matrix from an n-element vector, which can exhaust memory.

The test calls PolynomialFitter.fit(double[] guess) which delegates to fit(ParametricUnivariateFunction, double[]), which then calls fit(int, ParametricUnivariateFunction, double[]), but we only have partial code snippets showing that fit(int maxEval, double[] guess) calls fit(int, ParametricUnivariateFunction, double[]).

Given the bug report's description and test size (40,000 points), the underlying optimizer (LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer) used inside PolynomialFitter is likely trying to handle a very large vector of parameters or weights corresponding to the data points. The bug describes that when a Weight class is used with a large number of weights, an nxn full matrix is created and copied, causing memory exhaustion.

This matrix is likely related to the optimizer's internal computation (Jacobian or Hessian approximations for the multivariate vector optimization). The optimizer tries to build a matrix of size proportional to the number of parameters squared, but since here the vector scales with data points, this becomes huge.

The test fails because with 40,000 points, the optimization step tries to construct or copy this full matrix, exhausting memory or causing performance failures, leading to failure either due to errors or assertion failures in the test.

Thus the root cause is that the new multivariate vector optimizers used inside PolynomialFitter/LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer fail to scale when fitting large data sets due to internal inefficient large matrix computations linked to the handling of Weight objects or parameter vectors.

The recent bug reports are not particularly related, so they can be ignored.

# Diagnosis

The failure in testLargeSample is due to the underlying multivariate vector optimizer inside PolynomialFitter (using LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer) creating and copying a full nxn matrix from the n-length weight vector when fitting large numbers of points. This internal behavior causes memory exhaustion and failure for large data sets (e.g. 40,000 points). The test fails because the optimizer cannot handle the large number of observed points efficiently, leading to errors or suboptimal fitting leading to assertion failures. The root cause is inefficiency in the optimizer's handling of large weights vectors, as described in the current bug report.

This explains why even simple polynomial fitting fails for large samples. The code in PolynomialFitter.fit delegates to the optimizer, which uses weights internally and causes this issue.

Recommend fixing the optimizer or its use of weights to avoid creating full nxn matrices or copying them unnecessarily for large vectors.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
